# skill-comply

> A Claude Code skill (MIT, v0.3.0) that measures whether coding agents actually follow skills and rules (agent-definition invocation cannot currently be observed: the child session has the Agent tool denied). Auto-generates test scenarios at 3 prompt strictness levels, runs agents, classifies their tool calls and text output via LLM, and reports compliance rates with full timelines.

Status: active, synced one way from the author's Claude Code harness (`scripts/sync-from-local.sh`); the same skill also ships in the [akc-cycle](https://github.com/shimo4228/akc-cycle) plugin as `/akc-cycle:skill-comply`, and this repository can trail the plugin between syncs.

## Core documentation

- [llms-full.txt](llms-full.txt): self-contained Q&A reference for AI agents (Project Facts, Prior Research, 9 question-form H2 sections)
- [README.md](README.md): human-facing narrative (install, how it works, v0.2.0 real-world results)
- [SKILL.md](skills/skill-comply/SKILL.md): full skill specification — spec generation, scenario levels, classification, grading, models
- [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md): release notes v0.1.0 → v0.2.0 → v0.3.0

## Architecture

- 6-stage pipeline: Spec Generation → Scenario Generation → Execution → Classification → Grading → Report
- 3 prompt strictness levels: **Supportive** (prompt explicitly mentions the skill), **Neutral** (skill not mentioned), **Competing** (prompt contradicts the skill)
- Model split: `--gen-model` (haiku default), `--model` (sonnet default, the agent under test in scenario execution), `--classifier-model` (sonnet, 300s timeout)
- pytest tests in `skills/skill-comply/tests/`

## Standard reference

- [Agent Skill specification](https://agentskills.io/specification): the Claude Code skill format used by this repo
- [Claude `-p` stream-json](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/cli-reference): the trace capture mechanism used during scenario execution
